scope: Six original challenging Year 1 Pure Maths questions, three trig in degrees and three elementary differentiation questions, 41 marks, one manual graph sketch. No Year 2 Maths, Mechanics or Statistics.
notes: Original problems, not AQA past-paper reproduction or official examiner mark scheme. Accept mathematically equivalent rearrangements and appropriate rounding; one trig graph requires manual inspection and must never be scored by keyword alone.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Solve a quadratic trigonometric equation in degrees
questions.prompt: Solve 2sin²θ − 3sinθ + 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ < 360°. Give every solution in degrees and show the method. [6 marks]
markPoints: Recognises the equation is quadratic in u=sinθ.
Obtains θ=30° and θ=150° from sinθ=1/2.
Obtains θ=90° from sinθ=1, listing the complete solution set.
questions.modelAnswer: Let u=sinθ. Then 2u²−3u+1=(2u−1)(u−1)=0. Hence sinθ=1/2 or sinθ=1. On 0°≤θ<360°, sinθ=1/2 gives θ=30° or 150°, and sinθ=1 gives θ=90°. The complete set is θ=30°, 90°, 150°. No additional quadrants satisfy either condition.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Cosine rule, triangle angles and exact area
questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB=8.0 cm, AC=12.0 cm and angle BAC=60°. Calculate (a) length BC, (b) the angles ABC and ACB, and (c) the area of triangle ABC. Show the cosine- and area-formula reasoning. [7 marks]
markPoints: Uses a valid sine or cosine rule to find angle ABC, avoiding the ambiguous sine-rule solution.
Finds exact area 24√3 cm² or ≈41.6 cm².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Sketch transformed sine graph in degrees and identify zeros
questions.prompt: For 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, sketch y=2sinθ−1 with a labelled vertical scale. Mark all intercepts with the θ-axis, the maximum and minimum, and the midline. Explain how its amplitude and vertical translation compare with y=sinθ. Draw the graph; written keywords alone cannot earn drawing marks. [7 marks]
markPoints: Draws a smooth sine-shaped curve for the whole 0° to 360° interval with correctly labelled axes.
Shows amplitude 2 (correct vertical scale or stated).
Identifies the midline y=−1 and the shift down by 1.
Marks the first zero at θ=30°.
Marks the second zero at θ=150°; graph correctly begins/ends at y=−1.
questions.modelAnswer: The graph is a sine curve with amplitude 2, unchanged period 360°, midline y=−1 and vertical displacement one unit down. It passes through (0°,−1), peaks at (90°,1), crosses the axis at (30°,0) and (150°,0), passes through (180°,−1), reaches (270°,−3), and ends at (360°,−1). The whole graph, scales and labelled points must be manually reviewed; the written description does not automatically award drawing marks.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Find and classify both stationary points of a cubic
questions.prompt: For f(x)=2x³−15x²+24x+7, find the exact coordinates of every stationary point and classify each as a local maximum or minimum. Show your differentiation and justification. [8 marks]
markPoints: Classifies (1,18) as a local maximum from f''(1)=−18 or the gradient sign.
Classifies (4,−9) as a local minimum from f''(4)=18 or the gradient sign.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate: f'(x)=6x²−30x+24=6(x−1)(x−4). Stationary points occur at x=1 and x=4. f(1)=2−15+24+7=18; f(4)=128−240+96+7=−9. Since f''(x)=12x−30, f''(1)=−18<0 so (1,18) is a local maximum. f''(4)=18>0 so (4,−9) is a local minimum. Equivalent correctly explained derivative-sign arguments earn classification marks.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Tangent and normal equations at a rational curve point
questions.prompt: The curve is y=3/x+2x² for x≠0. Find the equations of the tangent and normal at x=1, giving each in the form y=mx+c. [6 marks]
markPoints: Differentiates using powers to get dy/dx=−3/x²+4x.
Finds the tangent gradient dy/dx at x=1 as 1.
Forms and simplifies the tangent y−5=1(x−1), so y=x+4.
Uses perpendicular gradients to find normal gradient −1.
Forms and simplifies the normal y−5=−(x−1), so y=−x+6.
questions.modelAnswer: Write y=3x⁻¹+2x², so dy/dx=−3x⁻²+4x. At x=1, y=3+2=5 and gradient=−3+4=1. The tangent has equation y−5=1(x−1), giving y=x+4. The normal gradient is the negative reciprocal, −1; y−5=−(x−1), so y=−x+6. A correctly equivalent line equation earns the same credit.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Determine parameters from a stationary point
questions.prompt: The curve f(x)=x³+ax²+bx+1 passes through (2,7) and has a stationary point when x=2. Find the exact values of a and b, then determine the nature of this stationary point. [7 marks]
markPoints: Uses the stationary condition f'(2)=0 to obtain 12+4a+b=0.
Solves the two simultaneous equations to give a=−11/2.
Finds f''(2)=12−11=1>0, so (2,7) is a local minimum.
questions.modelAnswer: Since f(2)=7, 8+4a+2b+1=7, giving 2a+b=−1. Differentiate: f'(x)=3x²+2ax+b. The stationary condition f'(2)=0 gives 12+4a+b=0, or 4a+b=−12. Subtracting 2a+b=−1 gives 2a=−11, so a=−11/2 and b=10. The second derivative is f''(x)=6x+2a, giving f''(2)=12−11=1>0, hence a local minimum at (2,7).
